platform: win32 10.0.26200, debug build in its isolated test mode (ADR 0003), WebView2 over CDP

build.how: npm run build, then cargo build (debug) on a clean tree at 70535c7; every phase ran this copy (exeSha256 in each phase)

summaryText: M0-05 final run, natively on Windows with Muse 1.4.2, on one build in its isolated test mode, 6 live turns, every item passed and no defect found. (1) A's exact question event copied into B: answering A with real clicks sent one answer_input, A's session only, and left both of B's cards as they were. (2) Two real questions waiting at once in A and B: A answered while B waited, B unchanged in the app and in its host, then B answered. (3) Skip clicked once: one cancel_input, the turn went on to its next question; Skip double-clicked on that one: still one cancel_input, no banner; the reply said first=SKIPPED second=SKIPPED. (4) One box for min_selections 2: refused -32057, the card kept the tick; the second box on the same card, no reload: accepted, reply GREEN+BLUE. (5) On this build: a question's engine killed with the app open (card removed, "Input cancelled: Muse stopped before you answered."), a restart with a question pending (no card, the cancel line once, idle a minute later), an approval pending at a force-kill ("Approval cancelled: Muse closed before you answered, so the action did not run." once, no card, no decision), a stale approval click (refused -32053, the calm notice, the card re-read on the current step).
forgedInputs: The folder dialog of "New project from a folder…" was answered by the harness for folders A and B: CDP cannot drive the OS dialog. Each conversation was started from the welcome screen with its first message.

Item 1 is forged: the host mints a fresh id per question, so a real collision cannot be produced. A's input_request event, as the bridge delivered it on poll_events, was copied with every field kept but session_id, set to B, and appended to the next poll_events response the renderer read: the path every bridge event takes (push_event, poll_events, pollOnce, handleEvent). It never reached the bridge or B's engine (B's host still listed only its own question). It wrote one more "Input requested" line in B's transcript. A window reload at the end removed the forged card, with no cancel line.
5a: the engine's death is a taskkill /F of the one engine child of the app whose working directory, read from its PEB, is folder A; B's engine kept running.
5c: the force-kill is a taskkill /F of the app process alone; both engines ended by themselves within 20 s; the harness killed none.

5d: the stale click is two single clicks (clickCount 1 each) dispatched back to back through CDP Input, 12 px apart: the page received two clicks of detail 1, 7 ms apart, not a double-click. The second landed before the card repainted the host's next stage, as a second click does when it lands between the host's advance and the repaint.

The page refuses a wrapper on __TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke (non-writable, non-configurable). Its calls were counted from the debugger: a conditional breakpoint on that function (Debugger.setBreakpointOnFunctionCall) whose condition records the command and returns false. answer_input, cancel_input and approve were also counted on window.fetch, the IPC transport; both counts agree in every phase that took them (pair, skip, stale-kill).

The harness read hosts through the app's list_pending_requests, which is not read-only: it also rebuilds the app's approval registry for the conversation read. Here it read only conversations with no approval pending (pair, q-death, b-restart: questions). stale-kill made no such read: the card's stage came from the tool_request events the bridge delivered (poll tap) and from the app's own re-read after the refusal.
No answer, skip, decision or message was forged: every pick, answer, skip and decision was a real mouse click through CDP Input, every message went through the composer or the welcome screen.
limits: The test mode isolates the app's data and WebView2 profile, not the engine's session store: the test conversations live in the engine's own store, as in the earlier isolated proofs.
After the resumes of q-death and b-restart the engine re-issued the dead question once; the app ignored it, as measured before (m0-05-complement.json).

q-death: "Muse stopped because the host process ended. Reconnect to continue." stays in the transcript although the app resumed the conversation by itself (resume on open), as recorded in m0-05-questions.json; not changed here.
5d: the calm notice stays in the banner until the next action clears it, by design.
notes: Isolation: one data folder (appdata-1) for the whole run, relaunches reused it; no WEBVIEW2_* variable; CDP on 9335; the WebView2 --user-data-dir checked under the data folder at every attach; MUSE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1; the exe ran from a copy. The instance ended closed from its window (stop-1.1); the only forced close was 5c's.

Harness: stale-kill's two decision verdicts were made independent of the order in which the host takes the two calls before the phase ran (48a87dd, its headAtPhase); the earlier phases ran on 4f006e5. The build did not change.
Order: launch, probe, pair, skip, q-death, b-restart, stale-kill, stop, final-summary. skip got both questions in one turn, so skip-double did not run.
